search_scope: Continuation of C9 fire 1's extensive open-literature sweep for a rights-clean pigment/filler volume-fraction viscosity ladder (eta vs phi at known/fittable phi_max) for an epoxy or model resin system. Fire 1 left 4 unexhausted directions in the data-acquisition-queue entry: (1) MDPI Coatings 12(10):1473 supplementary files, (2) Zenodo/Figshare dataset search, (3) ASTM purchase dead-end, (4) author contact. This fire pursued (1) and (2) and broadened the sweep to PMC, RSC Advances, Wiley, De Gruyter, Scientific Reports/Nature, and arXiv.

sources_checked_this_fire.source: Wiley 10.1002/adem.202301630 (Reynolds, Unterhalter, Francoeur, Bortner, Raeymaekers 2024, Advanced Engineering Materials 26(10):2301630, 'Viscosity of Mono- and Polydisperse Mixtures of Photopolymer and Rigid Spheres for Manufacturing of Engineered Composite Materials Using Vat Photopolymerization')
sources_checked_this_fire.method: Unpaywall API found a Virginia Tech VTechWorks institutional-repository OA copy (https://hdl.handle.net/10919/140523); fetched and ran pdftotext -layout on the full PDF.
sources_checked_this_fire.result: GENUINE HIT for content: paper experimentally measures apparent viscosity of a photopolymer resin (vat-photopolymerization/stereolithography resin, i.e. a UV-cure resin system analogous in kind to a reactive coating resin, though NOT itself a two-part epoxy-amine) filled with rigid glass microspheres, sweeping particle volume fraction Phi, particle size ratio, mono- vs polydispersity, shear rate, and temperature; fits the Krieger and Dougherty (1959) model explicitly (multiple direct citations, e.g. 'we superimpose the Krieger and Dougherty[48] model', with Phi_m maximum random packing density reported to decrease with increasing particle size ratio, Phi* ~= Phi_m = 0.54 for simple-cubic packing cited as a bound) and reports fitted intrinsic viscosity / fluidity-limit parameters. This is exactly the eta-vs-phi ladder with a fitted phi_max that C9's objective is looking for.
sources_checked_this_fire.license_finding: BLOCKED. The paper's own copyright/license line (page 1, under the author affiliations) reads verbatim: 'This is an open access article under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs License, which permits use and distribution in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited, the use is non-commercial and no modifications or adaptations are made.' This is CC BY-NC-ND, not CC BY. It is the *article* (Advanced Engineering Materials, Wiley-VCH), not a data-descriptor deposit, so the ND clause covers the reported data tables/figures as part of the licensed work.

why_this_is_a_rights_block_not_a_data_wa: A genuine, on-scope-adjacent (model UV-cure resin + rigid filler, explicit Krieger-Dougherty fit with phi_max) candidate dataset EXISTS and was located. The blocker is not absence of data (BLOCKED_DATA) but the license terms of the located asset (BLOCKED_RIGHTS): CC BY-NC-ND forbids (a) 'modifications or adaptations' -- extracting the paper's eta(phi) values into a re-typeset JSON table, computing our own KD fit residuals against them, and publishing that comparison as a portfolio benchmark receipt is a plausible 'adaptation' of the licensed content under a strict reading; and (b) 'non-commercial' use only -- Amphora's coating-IP portfolio is a commercial venture, so even a purely internal AUDIT_ONLY benchmark receipt is arguably 'commercial use' of the licensed material under a strict reading. Per governance rule 5 (never derive from quarantined sources; rights review is a human step), this cron does not resolve that ambiguity and does not extract, transcribe, or benchmark against Reynolds et al. 2024's actual data values. No numeric values from the paper are reproduced anywhere in this receipt or its artifacts -- only the paper's own already-public abstract-level statements (Phi_m ~ 0.54 bound, Phi < 0.05 / Phi = 0.25 breakpoints) are quoted verbatim and attributed, for identification purposes only, consistent with ordinary scholarly citation.
human_action_needed: (1) Legal/rights review of whether CC BY-NC-ND permits an internal, non-distributed, audit-only quantitative comparison receipt (arguably not a 'derivative' of the article itself, since it would use extracted numeric facts rather than reproduce the article's expression) -- if cleared, a follow-up fire can extract Reynolds et al. 2024's eta(phi) data and benchmark KRIEGER_DOUGHERTY against it. (2) In parallel/alternative: contact corresponding authors (mbortner@vt.edu, bart.raeymaekers@vt.edu) for explicit permission to use the underlying data for non-distributed internal benchmarking, or ask whether the underlying raw data is separately deposited (e.g. VTechWorks dataset, not just the article PDF) under a more permissive license.
not_extracted: No table values, figure-digitized points, phi_max fitted constant, or intrinsic-viscosity fitted constant from Reynolds et al. 2024 appear anywhere in this finding or in any file under this evidence/audit directory.
